Kenya reports second death from Ebola

Reuters

24 October, 2026 02:00 am IST

NAIROBI, Oct 23 (Reuters) – Kenya has recorded a second Ebola death, the health ministry said late on Friday, adding that the 65-year-old woman had developed symptoms during quarantine and was a close relative of a Kenyan man who died of Ebola earlier this month.

The outbreak, which started in the Democratic Republic of Congo, has now been reported in four countries across eastern, central and western Africa, giving it the widest geographic spread of any Ebola outbreak on the continent to date.

Kenya’s first Ebola case was identified this month in a man who travelled from Congo to Nairobi and died at a Nairobi hospital on October 5.

Show Full Article

Since then, Kenyan authorities have traced 135 contacts, all of whom were placed in quarantine, with nine cases confirmed.

The Ebola victim who died on Friday evening was a direct contact of the index patient, the ministry said.

“This loss brings the number of deaths to two among the nine confirmed cases. The remaining seven patients continue to receive care in the two isolation facilities,” the ministry said, adding there was no evidence of community spread in the country.

Late on Monday, the US State Department advised Americans to reconsider travel to Kenya and raised its travel advisory level for the country because of health risks.

On Tuesday, Nigeria became the fourth African country to report an Ebola case, with officials scrambling to work out how and where the patient, who had not travelled to the Democratic Republic of Congo, contracted the disease.

Ebola has infected nearly 10,000 people and killed more than 4,600 in Congo. The disease can cause fever, vomiting, diarrhoea and, in severe cases, internal and external bleeding. Only people with symptoms can transmit the virus.

The rare Ebola species behind the current outbreak has no approved treatment or vaccine.

(Reporting by Vincent Mumo Nzilani; writing by George Obulutsa; Editing by Daniel Wallis)

Russia, Ukraine agree to ceasefire in Ukrainian city hit by food crisis, brokered by Melania Trump

Reuters

23 October, 2026 10:00 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

(c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

By Steve Holland and Ryan Patrick Jones WASHINGTON, Oct 23 (Reuters) – US first lady Melania Trump has secured a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the Russian-controlled city of Oleshky, which will begin on October 29, the White House said on Friday.

Residents of the southern Ukrainian city, occupied by Russian forces since February 2022, have reported a deepening food crisis.

“Both nations agreed to temporarily stop all military action in Oleshky to allow for humanitarian aid to enter and to prepare a civilian evacuation through a designated safe passageway,” a White House statement said.

Show Full Article

Ukraine’s top negotiator, David Arakhamia, said on Telegram that the humanitarian operation would start once a ceasefire was in place.

He said the accord, the result of a long process involving Melania Trump and Pope Leo, would set up a humanitarian corridor for residents to leave and allow assistance into the town.

In Moscow, the Kremlin welcomed the agreement and said it would take a few days to work out a ceasefire. It praised Melania Trump’s role in securing the agreement and said President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin had discussed details.

Neither side provided additional details on the operation.

The Kremlin said earlier this week that work was under way to ease the humanitarian situation in Oleshky after Putin told the pope he was ready to cooperate on the issue.

The development comes as President Trump pressures Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy to reach an agreement with Putin to end the war, which began when Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022.

FIRST LADY HAS SOUGHT TO HELP UKRAINIAN CHILDREN

Melania Trump has been active in trying to get Ukrainian children seized by Russia during the war returned to their families.

“The situation in Oleshky is dire. Oleshky is a front-line war city on the brink of disaster. Oleshky’s remaining population is comprised primarily of elderly residents who urgently need medical attention, medicine, food, and clean water,” Melania Trump said in the statement.

The ceasefire will allow non-military teams from both countries to visit residents in their homes and coordinate transportation for those wishing to evacuate to either Russia or Ukraine, with an unnamed American media organization accompanying the teams to document the process, the first lady said.

Newsmax, a right-leaning news outlet, said in a report that its cameras would be granted “exclusive access to document the effort.”

Oleshky, located across the Dnipro River from the Ukrainian-held city of Kherson, has a remaining population of 1,700 to 2,000 people — primarily elderly residents, along with about 50 children — down from roughly 24,000 before the war, the White House said. About 90% of the city was flooded following the destruction of the Kakhovka Dam, according to the White House.

The statement said Melania Trump and her representative worked directly with Russian and Ukrainian leadership to define the terms of the localized ceasefire.

“Residents who wish to evacuate will receive coordinated support and transportation to their preferred destination. I anticipate some will want to go to Russia, and some to Ukraine,” Melania Trump said.

(Reporting by Steve Holland and Susan Heavey; Writing by Ryan Patrick Jones in Toronto; Editing by Katharine Jackson, David Ljunggren, Caitlin Webber, Rod Nickel and Ron Popeski)
